title: add downgrade guard, version pinning, and backup/restore hooks for private-installer upgrade path
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added automatic downgrade guard checks and backup/restore integration for private-installer upgrades. No API changes. Recommended: run backup before upgrade; new migration path is safe with rollback guard.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments using the on-prem installer have hit edge cases during upgrades where schema migrations partially applied and a subsequent downgrade caused data inconsistencies. This PR adds three coordinated pieces to make upgrades safer for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers: 1) a downgrade guard that prevents rolling back past migrations that would lose data, 2) version pinning for migration-aware components to ensure compatible rollbacks, and 3) hooks to perform pre-upgrade backup and post-rollback restore using the existing backup-restore tooling.

This change set includes: - operational scripts (bin/verify-downgrade-guard.sh) used by the installer to validate downgrade safety - helm chart changes to add pre-upgrade/post-rollback lifecycle hooks that call the backup/restore job templates - terraform module updates to expose version pinning flags and to record migration metadata in state for auditability - database migration metadata table (migration_history) population and checks in the installer to decide whether a downgrade is allowed - documentation and release notes for private customers and operators.

Implementation notes: - The downgrade guard is conservative: it refuses a downgrade if the migration_history shows applied migrations that the target older version does not know how to reverse. The guard provides an escape hatch (force flag) but logs a detailed audit entry and requires operator confirmation. - Version pinning is implemented via installer/envars and the terraform variable redwood_component_version_{component}, defaulting to the release manifest version. Pinning is read by the helm charts and the installer to select compatible image tags. - Backup/restore hooks call the existing backup-restore helm job. The pre-upgrade hook runs a snapshot and validates checksum; the post-rollback hook attempts restore if a rollback occurs. All hook invocations are idempotent.

Testing and validation: - End-to-end upgrade tests added to perf-canary (canary-upgrade-workflow) validating backup snapshotting and the guard preventing an unsafe rollback. - Unit tests for the downgrade guard logic and migration metadata parsing. - Manual upgrade on staging private cluster with seeded data sets to verify no data loss and that guard blocks intentional unsafe downgrades.

How to test locally: 1) Install private-installer against a staging cluster with sample data. 2) Run the installer upgrade path to a version that applies a migration. 3) Attempt a downgrade using the older installer image; the guard should block. 4) Use the --force-downgrade for a controlled test and verify the post-rollback restore runs and data is restored from the backup snapshot.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main, cut a minor release for private-installer. - Release notes will call out the required pre-upgrade backup step (automated by the hook by default). - Recommend customers to run the installer with version pinning enabled during staged rollouts.

Related: Linear ENG-8945, ENG-9012; Support ticket SUP-312 for an in-field upgrade incident that motivated this work.

Checklist: - [x] downgrade guard script - [x] helm lifecycle hooks - [x] terraform variable exposure + state metadata - [x] unit + e2e tests - [x] docs and release notes
commits: Add downgrade guard script and unit tests - initial implementation
Hook backup/restore pre/post lifecycle job into helm chart
Expose redwood_component_version_* in terraform private module and persist migration metadata
Add migration_history population and checks in installer upgrade path
Add e2e canary upgrade test and docs
review_comments: Michael Chen: Can you make the downgrade guard behaviour configurable? Some enterprise customers want a stricter no-force policy. (reply) Aisha: Added --require-approval and operator audit log entry; default remains conservative.

Sofia Martinez: The helm hook must be idempotent; what if the backup job fails transiently? (reply) Aisha: Hook retries 3x and writes a status ConfigMap; installer aborts only after exhausting retries.

Rajesh Gupta: Add a feature flag so we can ship without forcing terraform rollout changes on existing clusters. (reply) Aisha: Added 'enable_migration_metadata' flag defaulting to false. Upgrade notes instruct operators to enable it when ready.
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after approvals from Michael and Sofia. Verified canary upgrade results and ran a staging rollback to validate restore path.
notes_for_ops: Operators: Backups are now automatic pre-upgrade by default. To disable automatic backups set charts.private-installer.backup.enabled=false. For emergency downgrades use installer --force-downgrade but be aware of potential irreversible migrations. Enable migration metadata in terraform to get audit trail in state.
short_description: Adds downgrade guard, version pinning and backup/restore helm hooks to make private-installer upgrades safer for on-prem deployments.
